name: CNS Infections Meningitis Encephalitis Long Case

reference.source: Long Cases in Clinical Medicine (topic map; text rewritten, no verbatim copy)
reference.pathophysiology: Bacterial invasion clouds CSF with neutrophils and low glucose demanding hours-fast ceftriaxone; herpes necrotises temporal lobes producing confusion and seizures answering acyclovir, and contiguous ear or sinus sepsis walls into ring-enhancing abscess.
additionalDifferentials: Bacterial versus viral versus TB versus abscess by cells glucose and ring
Meningitis versus encephalitis by consciousness and temporal signs
Meningococcal versus viral rash by glass test
